newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Hun Sen's forces inch towards royalist stronghold.
newsitem.headline: Hun Sen's forces inch towards royalist stronghold.

text.p: Cambodian forces loyal to strongman Hun Sen on Wednesday inched their way toward this last town held by royalist troops, with some mortar rounds landing for the first time inside the town, residents said.

Exchanges were clearly audible in this border town, the last major redoubt of forces loyal to prime Prince Norodom Ranariddh in retreat since a bloody coup in Phnom Penh removed him from power more than a month ago.
In Phnom Penh, defence ministry spokesman Colonel Chum Sambath said government forces were getting closer to O'Smach.
"We've been getting closer and closer (to O'Smach) over the last few days," he told Reuters.
A wife of a royalist soldier here said there was fighting near Kron Krian village, about 18 km (12 miles) to the south.
"Right now the situation is not clear yet but Hun Sen's troops have captured Chhkung village," said Petch Nari, 35, a mother of two. Chhkung is about 20 km (13 miles) south of here.
Since ousting Ranariddh on July 6 Hun Sen has battled the prince for diplomatic approval overseas while pushing the ragged remnants of his army to remote pockets of the country.
Many royalist officials and supporters have fled to Thailand after the coup and a subsequent crackdown in which some 40 of the prince's supporters were killed.
Only O'Smach and a few villages remain in the hands of forces opposing Hun Sen, some of them controlled by the rump of the Khmer Rouge which ruled Cambodia between 1975 and 1979.

Defence ministry spokesman Chum Sambath said he was confident government forces would capture O'Smach as well as the Khmer Rouge headquarters at Anlong Veng to the east, and said his side was appealing to opponents to give up and defect.
"We use a strategy of appealing to them to join with the government," he said in Phnom Penh.
Ranariddh has vowed to continue his political and armed struggle despite setbacks on both fields.
Predictions that O'Smach would fall to Hun Sen forces have proved premature as his soldiers pick their way through booby traps and landmines lain by retreating Ranariddh forces.
Panicking Cambodians in O'Smach came out of their houses and watched mortar firing on the main road on Wednesday before fleeing when mortar rounds landed near the town centre.
It was believed to be the first time that mortar rounds had landed inside the town. It was not known if the mortar fire caused casualties.
Shelling eased in the late afternoon on Wednesday, although still many Cambodians, their belongings packed and ready for evacuation, hid their families or dug bunkers in the ground.
"I have no place to go, and my mother is very old. We have to hide ourselves here," said Ton Chia, a merchant.
Thai soldiers closed the border at Chung Chon Pass but said they would evacuate refugees if the situation worsened.
"We have a plan to evacuate them to a safe place in Thailand, if we see the situation is bad. But now is not a proper time to take them in," said an army colonel.
